newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page - Mar 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page - Mar 7.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Friday:
WASHINGTON - Faced with choosing between a wide-ranging probe of campaign fund-raising practices and its own desire for self-preservation, the Senate found a way to have it both ways.
WASHINGTON - A key House committee voted overwhelmingly to override President Clinton's decision to certify Mexico as cooperating with U.S. anti-drug efforts.
WASHINGTON - D.C. Council chairman David Clarke, who has been hospitalized for nearly three months, is seriously ill with a degenerative neurological disorder and can barely speak.

WASHINGTON - As states begin remaking their welfare programs, several are turning over whole sections of their bureaucracies to private industry, a move that could eliminate tens of thousands of government jobs.

LITTLE ROCK - Attorney Joseph Giroir, a former law partner of Hillary Rodham Clinton and behind-the-scenes Arkansas dealmaker, draws heat for his international links in the campaign fund-raising flap.
MOSCOW - President Boris Yeltsin formally returned to the political arena vowing to "create order" out of economic chaos and political corruption but blaming others for Russia's deepening decay.
